canonical_statement: The study aimed to evaluate reusable agent-skill quality at the SKILL.md document level using interpretable intrinsic signals that complement downstream task evaluation.
SkillEval decomposes skill quality into four dimensions: applicability, content quality, execution guidance, and robustness.
A1 Format Validity, under Applicability, evaluates whether a skill is a Markdown file with valid YAML frontmatter and required name and description fields.
A2 Trigger Clarity, under Applicability, evaluates whether the description states what the skill does, when it should be used, and its main applicability conditions.
B1 Content Consistency, under Content Quality, evaluates whether capabilities stated in the description are supported by instructions and resources in the body.
B2 Technical Specificity, under Content Quality, evaluates whether the skill provides concrete executable details such as tools, commands, parameters, fields, units, constraints, and file paths.
C1 Workflow Integrity, under Execution Guidance, evaluates whether the skill specifies the required input, processing, and output stages.
C2 I/O Explicitness, under Execution Guidance, evaluates whether expected inputs and outputs, formats, fields, schemas, units, and constraints are explicitly defined.
D1 Failure Awareness, under Robustness, evaluates whether the skill covers common failures, boundary conditions, diagnostic signals, and recovery strategies.

For each learned semantic metric, the authors construct controlled positive-negative skill pairs intended to differ mainly in the target quality property while preserving task goal, topic, tools, and other content as much as possible.
The main SkillEval scorer uses a frozen Qwen3.5-9B model and extracts hidden-state representations at index 16.

Metric-specific pooling uses the frontmatter description for A2, the average of description and body representations for B1, mean body pooling for B2/C1/C2, and the final token of the full model input for D1.
The main representation pipeline permits up to 20,000 input tokens, and no document in the dataset was truncated.
For each metric, pairwise representation differences are orthogonalized against a precomputed confounding direction, averaged, and normalized to form the fixed metric direction.
A new skill is scored by projecting its pooled representation onto the fixed metric direction and converting the projection to a z-score using positive and negative training-skill statistics.
The SkillEval dataset contains 1,647 skills drawn from open-source datasets, public online sources, manual construction, and LLM generation.

population.label: Skill documents used by SkillEval

canonical_statement: For each semantic metric, controlled skill pairs are split into training and validation sets with no overlap in original documents, tasks, sources, or generation templates; directions and normalization statistics are learned only from training data.

Downstream evaluation uses SkillsBench with Codex using GPT-5.5 at xhigh reasoning effort; with-skill and no-skill conditions share the same environment and executor configuration, and each condition is evaluated over three runs.
Pass-rate uplift is defined as the pass rate with a skill minus the pass rate without a skill.

outcome.definition: Pass rate with skill minus pass rate without skill

Each learned semantic metric uses a separate dataset assembled from LLM-generated skills, publicly collected skills, and controlled positive-negative pairs; related examples retain the source-task data split to prevent train-validation overlap.

source_anchor.paragraph: Metric-Specific Dataset Construction — Data Sources and Common Procedure

canonical_statement: For A2 Trigger Clarity controlled negatives, only the frontmatter description is rewritten from a clear trigger condition to a general capability description while the body and other frontmatter fields remain unchanged and description length is kept similar.

For B1 Content Consistency controlled negatives, the original frontmatter is preserved while the body is replaced by a body from a different skill, with approximate body length matched where possible.

For B2 Technical Specificity controlled negatives, an LLM replaces concrete technical details with general descriptions while preserving frontmatter, task topic, main workflow, input-output setting, overall structure, and approximate length.

For C1 Workflow Integrity controlled negatives, the procedure is weakened by reordering dependent steps, removing important transitions, replacing ordered procedures with unordered suggestions, or making the input-to-output path incomplete while retaining task, tools, and most technical details.

For C2 I/O Explicitness controlled negatives, explicit formats, fields, keys, schemas, units, types, and output details are removed or generalized while frontmatter, task, tools, APIs, and main workflow are preserved and large deletions are avoided.

For D1 Failure Awareness controlled negatives, rule-based processing removes complete failure-related sections and standalone warnings, after which an LLM minimally edits embedded failure-related clauses while preserving frontmatter and unrelated procedural content.

The authors conclude that reusable skill quality has two complementary aspects—compatibility with a particular task and general document properties that support reuse—and that SkillEval provides interpretable document-level signals informative of downstream utility.
